note: Fallback people-lines for juice events whose payload carries no line. Short, in-voice, never shaming. `lines` are plain lists (read as lists by sim modules); `talk` keys are a list or a grammar {frames, rules} expanded by sim/grammar.ts, with the shared `rules` below.

start.den_near_hills: You're the one from the den under the hill. The little ones say you hum to the coals.
Saw your smoke on the hill again. Come down slow, the goats spook.
start.den_near_hills.self: The den is warm and the hill is quiet. Time to go down and knock.
Coal's banked. Somebody down there needs a bigger door than they've got.
start.ledger_office: You'll be the clerk. The ledger office is the door with the book on its sign.
Biggest town on the road and nobody's added the books up in a year. Welcome.
start.ledger_office.self: Biggest town, biggest ledger. Somebody here owes somebody the truth.
Ink's dry, nib's sharp. Let's see who's been signing for what.
start.warm_rock: Three of you on the warm rock again. Don't stare at the goats.
The rock by the road's been warm since dawn. I suppose that's yours.
start.warm_rock.self: The rock still holds the sun. We'll go in when it cools.
One of us watches the lane, one the doors, one the hearth. Then we go in.
start.mill_row: Bren? From the row? Sit, there's the heel of a loaf left.
The wheel's still, but the row remembers you. Bread's on the sill.
start.mill_row.self: The mill's quiet. Somebody on this row still bakes, though. I can smell it.
Two cups on the step. Maybe today someone drinks the second.
body.lift_wagon: You get a shoulder under the axle and lift. The wheel comes up out of the rut and the oxen pull. The driver presses coins on you.
The wagon rocks, then rises. You set it down on the hard road. The driver laughs and pays you for it.
body.lift_wagon.heard: Did you see that? Lifted a loaded wagon like a basket.
The wagon was stuck to the hubs, and up it came. Gently, too.
body.carry_crates: You take three crates at once and walk them into the store. The driver shakes their head and pays you a coin.
The heavy crates go in on your back. The unloading's half done before the driver's had a drink.
body.carry_crates.heard: Crates came in faster than I could count them. That was you?
The big one carried the whole wagon in. The stores look fuller already.
body.read_ledger: The ledger: {cover}. {short} In the margin, {who}'s name, underlined twice.
You read down the columns: {cover}. {short} One name keeps turning up owing: {who}.
body.read_ledger.heard: You read that like it was a letter from home.
Nobody's read those columns aloud since the reeve left. Go on, who's short?
body.watch_left: {body} curls up by the {place}, eyes half open.
body.watch_report.board: {body}, watching the noticeboard in {town}, saw {who} read the shortage notice twice. They're short of {item}.
{body} kept the noticeboard in {town}: {who} stood there a long while over the {item} notice.
body.watch_report.hearth: {body} kept the hearth in {town} all night. {who} sat closest to the coals and never said a word.
{body}, by the hearth in {town}, watched {who} feed it the last of their kindling.
body.watch_report.quiet: {body}, watching the noticeboard in {town}, saw {who} read every notice and nod. Nothing's short there.
{body} kept the noticeboard in {town}: {who} pinned up a thank-you and went home.
entry.vent: {body} squeezes through the vent under the eaves.
entry.yard: You come in by the yard gate, stooping under the lintel.
In through the yard, past the barrels.
entry.office: The clerk lifts the counter flap for you. Ink and dust.
Someone with business on paper. They let you through.
entry.refused.office: The clerk shakes their head. Offices are for people with business on paper.
The ledger office keeps its counter shut to you.
food_starve: the larders are bare, and folk went to bed hungry last night.
there wasn't bread enough to go round last night. The children ate first.
food_short: there's only {days} of food left in the stores.
the stores are thin: {days} of food, if nobody is greedy.
food_eased: the larders are filling again. Nobody went hungry last night.
there's food enough in the stores now. Folk are breathing easier.
workshop_unpaid: no wage came from your {building} this morning.
the till at your {building} was empty again. That's {days} unpaid.
workshop_quit: there's been no wage from your {building} in {days}. That's the end of it.
nobody works for nothing. {days} unpaid, and done with your {building}.
dawn_inherited_dependence_held: {who} says you lean on people the way {prev} did.
{who} says you still reach for a hand, like {prev} taught you.
dawn_inherited_dependence_resolved: {who} says you stand on your own now. {prev}'s need has let go of you.
{who} says something in you steadied overnight. You don't need {prev}'s crutch anymore.

hedge: Or that's how it looks to me.
town_talk: It's all the talk at the well.

town_talk.text: In all my years I've not seen the like.
My mam says not to listen. I listen.
Folk at the ovens talked of nothing else.
The inn's been full of it.
It came up at the forge before the fire was hot.
The boats came in full of it.

close_warm: Sit a minute, if you like.

close_warm.text: I'm at the bench most days, if you want me.
There's a heel of bread for you, if you come by.

close_hard: I'd not linger, if I were you.
after_deep: Give me a moment with it.
I'll be turning that over all night.
